decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 0.75% to 1%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Neel Kashkari.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in February indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activ…”

changes.quote: Job gains remained solid and the unemployment rate was little changed in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains remained solid and the unemployment rate stayed near its recent low.”

changes.quote: Household spending has continued to rise moderately while business fixed investment appears to have firmed somewhat.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has continued to rise moderately while business fixed investment has remained soft.”

changes.quote: Inflation has increased in recent quarters, moving close to the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective; excluding energy and food prices, inflation was little changed and continued to run somewhat below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation increased in recent quarters but is still below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective.”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.”

changes.quote: Measures of consumer and business sentiment have improved of late.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3/4 to 1 percent.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.41% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.51% and moved -9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.1% would fall by about $15.62 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.6%, and employers added an average of 221k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.8% over the past year (February 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -7 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.84%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 72%, cut 0%, hike 28%.
